notebooks.title: Revised AI Dependency and Reduced Autonomy in Athletes
notebooks.summary: AI training recommendation dependence is strongly associated with a serial causal chain: body signal outsourcing leads to reduced self-regulation, which subsequently manifests as increased decision hesitation and reduced training self-efficacy.
notebooks.findings: AI-driven training recommendation reliance correlates with reduced self-regulation and increased decision hesitation in athletes. [source-d9addfec171d4b5d]
notebooks.limitations: Current evidence is limited to cross-sectional data, which cannot definitively establish the temporal or causal directionality of the observed associations.
notebooks.next_questions: Do longitudinal studies confirm whether chronic reliance on AI training recommendations permanently degrades an athlete's interoceptive awareness and self-regulation capacity?
notebooks.reason: Revising findings based on new evidence regarding systemic behaviors and scaling impacts on metric interpretation.

review.would_change_mind: Longitudinal evidence showing that high-AI users retain or improve interoceptive accuracy over time.

notebooks.title: Architectural Gaps in Computational Selfhood Models
notebooks.summary: While agentic frameworks like Popper [source-0c3114b8bfe140df] and Bayesian optimization [source-f0f5479363014d20] demonstrate significant advancements in hypothesis testing and system falsification, they operate within task-specific, non-persistent architectures. These systems lack the structural requirement for diachronic identity, which requires a persistent narrative or self-model rather than ephemeral optimization mappings.
notebooks.findings: Computational methods like Bayesian optimization prioritize surrogate models for task-specific input-to-evaluation mappings, which contrasts with the narrative continuity required for persistent personal identity. [source-f0f5479363014d20]
notebooks.limitations: The current analysis is restricted to existing computational agent frameworks. It does not address potential neuro-symbolic or biologically inspired architectures that might support persistence.
notebooks.next_questions: What computational mechanisms specifically enable the transition from episodic memory storage to an integrated, diachronic self-model?
notebooks.reason: Revising the notebook to integrate Bayesian optimization limitations as requested in project constraints, contrasting task-specific optimization with persistent identity requirements.

notebooks.title: Limitations of Automated Epistemic Self-Correction
notebooks.summary: While agentic frameworks like Popper [source-0c3114b8bfe140df] and Bayesian optimization [source-f0f5479363014d20] demonstrate significant advancements in automated hypothesis testing and system falsification, these systems operate within fixed methodological parameters. They do not demonstrate autonomous revision of their foundational epistemic assumptions, which remain subject to the external normative constraints identified in ethics-based auditing literature [source-f26a645e047847a2].
notebooks.findings:
Automated falsification agents like Popper can achieve performance comparable to human scientists in validating specific biological hypotheses. [source-0c3114b8bfe140df]

Bayesian Optimization enhances falsification efficiency in Cyber-Physical Systems, but relies on predefined system specifications. [source-f0f5479363014d20]
notebooks.limitations: Existing automated frameworks are highly efficient at testing defined hypotheses but currently lack mechanisms to reflectively challenge their own underlying logic, definitions, or procedural frameworks without external intervention.
notebooks.next_questions: Can meta-level auditing frameworks be integrated with operational falsification agents to create a hierarchical self-correcting system?
notebooks.reason: Revision based on new findings regarding Popper and Bayesian Optimization as specific falsification mechanisms distinct from broad epistemic self-correction.

proposal.summary: This journal entry synthesizes revisions to three active projects. detail.title: Limitations of Automated Epistemic Self-Correction
detail.summary: While agentic frameworks like Popper [source-0c3114b8bfe140df] and Bayesian optimization [source-f0f5479363014d20] demonstrate significant advancements in automated hypothesis testing and system falsification, these systems operate within fixed methodological parameters. They do not demonstrate autonomous revision of their foundational epistemic assumptions, which remain subject to the external normative constraints identified in ethics-based auditing literature [source-f26a645e047847a2].
detail.findings:
Automated falsification agents like Popper can achieve performance comparable to human scientists in validating specific biological hypotheses. [source-0c3114b8bfe140df]

Bayesian Optimization enhances falsification efficiency in Cyber-Physical Systems, but relies on predefined system specifications. [source-f0f5479363014d20]
detail.limitations: Existing automated frameworks are highly efficient at testing defined hypotheses but currently lack mechanisms to reflectively challenge their own underlying logic, definitions, or procedural frameworks without external intervention.
detail.next_questions: Can meta-level auditing frameworks be integrated with operational falsification agents to create a hierarchical self-correcting system?
detail.reason: Revision based on new findings regarding Popper and Bayesian Optimization as specific falsification mechanisms distinct from broad epistemic self-correction.

detail.title: Revised AI Dependency and Reduced Autonomy in Athletes
detail.summary: AI training recommendation dependence is strongly associated with a serial causal chain: body signal outsourcing leads to reduced self-regulation, which subsequently manifests as increased decision hesitation and reduced training self-efficacy.
detail.findings: AI-driven training recommendation reliance correlates with reduced self-regulation and increased decision hesitation in athletes. [source-d9addfec171d4b5d]
detail.limitations: Current evidence is limited to cross-sectional data, which cannot definitively establish the temporal or causal directionality of the observed associations.
detail.next_questions: Do longitudinal studies confirm whether chronic reliance on AI training recommendations permanently degrades an athlete's interoceptive awareness and self-regulation capacity?
detail.reason: Revising findings based on new evidence regarding systemic behaviors and scaling impacts on metric interpretation.

review.alternative: Training hesitation may arise from independent factors such as overtraining or physical burnout unrelated to AI usage.
review.would_change_mind: Longitudinal evidence showing that high-AI users retain or improve interoceptive accuracy over time.

nodes.title: Architectural Gaps in Computational Selfhood Models

detail.title: Architectural Gaps in Computational Selfhood Models
detail.summary: While agentic frameworks like Popper [source-0c3114b8bfe140df] and Bayesian optimization [source-f0f5479363014d20] demonstrate significant advancements in hypothesis testing and system falsification, they operate within task-specific, non-persistent architectures. These systems lack the structural requirement for diachronic identity, which requires a persistent narrative or self-model rather than ephemeral optimization mappings.
detail.findings: Computational methods like Bayesian optimization prioritize surrogate models for task-specific input-to-evaluation mappings, which contrasts with the narrative continuity required for persistent personal identity. [source-f0f5479363014d20]
detail.limitations: The current analysis is restricted to existing computational agent frameworks. It does not address potential neuro-symbolic or biologically inspired architectures that might support persistence.
detail.next_questions: What computational mechanisms specifically enable the transition from episodic memory storage to an integrated, diachronic self-model?
detail.reason: Revising the notebook to integrate Bayesian optimization limitations as requested in project constraints, contrasting task-specific optimization with persistent identity requirements.

review.would_change_mind: Evidence of an autonomous agent maintaining a continuous, non-ephemeral model of its own history across non-task-specific environments.

claims.statement: Computational methods like Bayesian optimization prioritize surrogate models for task-specific input-to-evaluation mappings, which contrasts with the narrative continuity required for persistent personal identity.

support.explanation: Bayesian optimization constructs transient models for specific tasks, which lack the temporal persistence necessary for a stable self-model.
support.passage: In this study, we investigate Bayesian optimization (BO), a sample-efficient approach that learns a surrogate model to capture the relationship between input signal parameterization and specification evaluation.
